title: Appointment Scheduling Policy on Future Appointments Held in One Department
content:
**Clause.** A patient may hold many **Appointment Scheduling** appointments at Riverbend Regional Health, but at most the visit type's figure for future appointments per department — future appointments that are booked or confirmed — in one department; a recurring infusion series books each chair session as its own appointment.

## What the clause means

- **No overall limit across the patient's appointments.** The clause sets no cap on the total number of appointments a patient holds; the limit applies department by department.
- **What is counted.** Only future appointments whose status is booked or confirmed count toward the figure. An appointment that has been checked in, completed, cancelled or marked no-show is not a booked or confirmed future appointment.
- **Where the figure comes from.** The figure is the future-appointments-per-department figure of the visit type, and it is applied to the appointments the patient holds in that visit type's department.
- **Infusion series.** In a recurring infusion series every chair session is booked as its own appointment, so each session is one future appointment in the department.

## Count table — hypothetical figure

The figure of 2 below is invented for illustration only; it is not the figure of any particular visit type.

| Booked or confirmed future appointments the patient already holds in the department | Holding one more in the same department | Within the limit of 2? |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | yes |
| 1 | 2 | yes |
| 2 | 3 | no |

## Points of judgement

**Does a future appointment in another department count toward the figure?** No. The figure limits future appointments in one department; an appointment in a different department is counted only in that other department.

**Does a past, completed appointment count?** No. Only future appointments that are booked or confirmed are counted.

**How does a hypothetical series of six infusion chair sessions count?** As six future appointments in the department, because each chair session is booked as its own appointment.
